commits.subject: Defer signed backup manifests (DB-10) until old backups stay restorable
commits.body:
Reverts c7bbd52b from this integration; the commit stays ready to apply.
As written it refuses every unsigned (v1) backup, so the day it deployed
every existing nightly and pre-deploy snapshot on the host would become
unrestorable by `deploy/karmax restore`, and recovery onto a fresh host
would newly require supplying the vault key separately. DB-10 is a LOW
finding (tampering needs write access to the backup directory). Signing
new manifests should ship with an explicit, audited path for restoring a
v1 backup and an updated recovery runbook.

commits.subject: Evict provider caches after sandbox destruction
commits.body: WD-3, PS-10: all successful teardown paths remove SDK objects and lifecycle map entries. Weak handle tombstones preserve status without retaining every historical sandbox.

finding: PS-11 MED/LOW broker.ts:27,82 — CredentialBroker.auditLog unbounded (~0.3 MB/day/org from mail polling). Fix: ring buffer.

commits.subject: Bound credential broker audit memory
commits.body: PS-11: Keep the newest 1000 credential resolution attempts in a ring so polling and long-lived broker processes cannot grow this diagnostic array without bound. Preserve chronological audit_log output.

finding: PS-12 LOW/MED server.ts:653-699, 8046-8065 — WebSocket close handlers registered after awaits → leaked fanout subscribers, timing polls, preview world pins + runner leases (world never parks, keeps billing). Fix: register once('close') before awaiting / re-check readyState.

commits.subject: Release socket resources acquired after disconnect
commits.body: PS-12: register lifecycle cleanup before asynchronous initialization. Timing subscribers, review streams and preview access leases are disposed even when their acquisition finishes after the browser has closed.

finding: PS-13 LOW per-event full hydration: collaboration routing getTask per view.updated (api.ts:4635), restart check loads all events (main.ts:693), delivery getTask + listUsers, fanout re-verifies the token per event per socket.

commits.subject: Project delivery envelopes from indexed task and user rows
commits.body: PS-13: Delivery polling needed only a task title/number and one recipient, yet hydrated the full task conversation and listed every identity user for each claim. Read the compact task header and primary-key user row instead. Cover SQLite delivery, identity lookup, and PostgreSQL lookup.

commits.subject: Avoid task hydration on routine collaboration and restart events
commits.body: PS-13: Route complete view.updated lifecycle payloads directly, falling back to the stored view only for incomplete historical payloads. Check for a merged result with an indexed EXISTS query rather than parsing every task event on each done update. Cover the hot paths and PostgreSQL parity.

finding: PS-14 LOW small unbounded structures: codex stderr kept whole, runners probedAt map, terminal tickets swept only on mint, legacy sessions map.

commits.subject: Evict stale world probe timestamps
commits.body: PS-14: Lifecycle probes retain one timestamp per world generation; prune entries after two reconciliation windows so destroyed or replaced worlds do not accumulate in a long-lived gateway. Cover sweep eviction without a paid provider.

commits.subject: Bound Codex stderr while retaining recent failures
commits.body: PS-14: Keep only the latest 4 KiB from app-server and legacy exec stderr streams, and include the recent diagnostic on failure. This prevents a long-lived turn from retaining unbounded provider stderr. Also correct fixture tuple types found by native typecheck.

finding: PS-15 LOW dev-server.ts:146-157,677 — health watcher opens a new gRPC connection every 15 s (late connects never closed); refreshManagedMcp rewrites every config home on each boot.

commits.subject: Reuse Temporal health connections and unchanged MCP files
commits.body: PS-15: retain one gRPC connection per watcher, close late connections after stop, and publish managed config only when its contents change.
